text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- The government decided to merge the police schools in Tallinn and in Paikuse, liquidate the internal defence unit that has assisted the police, and make changes in the structure of the police department from August 1.
- The interior minister appointed Peet Kall as acting police prefect of Tallinn.
- In 1996, 48 persons in Estonia declared income of over one million kroons. Ten of them earned over two million, tax officials said.
- The government signed an agreement with farmers on a 549 million kroon subsidy for agriculture in the 1998 budget.
- Hansapank increased its profit forecast for its group from 320 to 475 million kroons.
- Svante Paabo, an Estonian by origin, was the leader of the group of scientists in Munich that proved by DNA that Homo Sapiens did not descend from the Neanderthal Man.
- Armenian Mushegh Grigoryan is the first person to formally apply for asylum in Estonia; the decision will be made in September, officials said.
- Tallinn Department Store plans to reorganise the largest shop in Tartu into a 2000 square metre modern store by the year 2000.
